name: linked-single-int-transpose-write
rationale: One dispatched invocation addresses one NDArray element. The reference-size and coordinate-mapping constants bound every dimension and stride to one; the linked prefix returns an exact nonzero value, the linked postfix writes it, and both callbacks are loop-free. Transpose variants use one initialized lane and the exact reflected dynamic threadgroup allocation.

name: linked-single-invocation-zero-bins
rationale: One invocation is bounded by source_size 1x1. The fixed channel loop advances its literal selector through the entry’s finite component count before exiting; it has no input-dependent trip count. Linking is enabled with one authored texture and one address-table element, while the exact callback returns float4 zero without dereferencing either resource. One-bin histogram parameters force each active channel to bin zero and make the poisoned counters observable byte-exactly.

name: vote-four-pixels-against-a-thirty-two-step-palette
rationale: The palette walk has a literal trip count of thirty-two and no input-dependent exit. Each thread narrows its ushort texel to bytes, swizzles it to BGR and scores five per palette entry within forty-five of it on all three channels. Two of the four texels carry a component above 255 so the ushort-to-uchar narrowing is observable rather than an identity, the palette is an even ramp so each pixel's score is a window width, and the fourth texel spreads its channels far enough apart that no entry can satisfy all three and it scores nothing. The four scores are distinct, so the poisoned target says which pixel produced which.

name: nan-model-fmod-zero-remainders-and-infinite-divisors-under-fast-math
rationale: nan_fmod_zero_fast (nan_fmod_zero's program under the default fast math: float fmod is air.fast_fmod, half fmod carries fast; DESIGN D293): lane i reads floats a, b and halves ha, hb (the same values where half holds them) and writes fmod(a, b), fmod(ha, hb), a, and b. Lanes: zero remainders of either dividend and divisor sign (fmod(2, 0.5), fmod(-1.5, 0.75), fmod(+-65504, +-65504), and k * d for k = +-1 to +-2048), zero dividends, infinite divisors (fmod(+-0, +-inf), fmod(+-1, +-inf), fmod(+-65504, +-inf)), nonzero remainders, fmod(1, 0) and fmod(inf, 1), and half and float denormal dividends and divisors. Every operand is loaded from a buffer; the output is pre-filled with 0xAB.

name: linked-single-unit-depthwise-gradient-finalize
rationale: One invocation covers one channel and a 1x1x1 kernel, with unit source, destination, stride, dilation, threadgroup-count, kernel-count, channel-multiplier, and reduction extents. Those literal unit fields bound every reachable channel, kernel, threadgroup, and reduction loop to one iteration. The direct, non-accumulating specialization reads the sole temporary float and the exact primary destination writes the finite result to the sole poisoned output; the exact accumulation callback remains linked but unreachable.

name: linked-k24-two-row-quantized-vector-matrix
rationale: Reaching variant of linked-zero-k cases of this entry (DESIGN D296), whose parameters stop the kernel before its arithmetic. One threadgroup of 32 lanes; the user constant keeps 8-bit unsigned weights, group size one, no bias; constant 122 binds a two-entry table (1 source, 1 destination). The parameters select two rows of x (vec_n_rows 2 in the user constant) against W's row 0 over K = 24: lanes 0 to 5 each dequantize four 8-bit values per row, the simdgroup sums each row, and lane 0 hands both rows' results to the linked destination callback, which writes them in turn to element index threadgroup_position.x = 0 of table entry 1 (4 bytes observed: the second row's result). x holds 1 to 5 repeating (so the two rows differ), the scales 0.5, 1, 2 repeating, the biases 0 to 3 repeating, and W small integers below 16, so every product and partial sum is an integer multiple of 0.5 far below 2^24: exact in any order or contraction.

name: linked-zero-k-quantized-vector-matrix
no_effect: The authored parameters give the work an empty extent, so the entry returns before any write reaches the selected output.
rationale: One invocation uses a one-element linked destination array. The authored user constant selects eight-bit quantization, group size one, and zero vector rows; the exact zero K parameter makes both accumulation counts zero. Every arithmetic loop and the final postfix loop is therefore zero-trip, so the poisoned linked destination remains byte-exact while the wrapper and linkage contract execute. Replaced (DESIGN D296): the linked destination callback writes table entry 1, so the case binds a two-entry table (MPSNDArrayRefSize 1 source, 1 destination) whose destination element carries the source element's fill.

name: every-texture-atomic-at-lane-zero-on-1d-1d-array-2d-array-3d-buffer-and-2d-textures
rationale: Every texture atomic D283 decodes (family C), each result read at lane 0, in a kernel: thread t works on texel t of texture 0 (r32_uint 1D, 8 wide, 0x1000 + 0x111t), 1 (r32_sint 1D array, 8 wide, 2 layers, (-1)^(t+l) (20 + 3t + 50l)), 2 (r32_uint 2D array, 8x1, 2 slices, 0x2000 + 0x10t + 0x100l), 3 (r32_sint 3D, 8x1x2, (-1)^t (1000 + 37t) + 500z), 4 (r32_uint buffer, 8, 0x4000 + t), and 5 (r32_sint 2D, 8x1, -5 + 2t; 16-bit coordinates), all read_write, at layer (or slice) t & 1, and 2 from thread 9: it fetch-adds, -subs, -ands, -ors, -xors, -mins, and -maxes, exchanges, stores, loads, and compare-exchanges with a stale and then the current expected texel (lane 0 of expected read back), writing each old texel's first component (as uint), each compare-exchange's result, and the layer to out[40t .. 40t + 39] of buffer 0 (uint elements, pre-filled with 0xAB). 8 threads, every texel inside its texture. The AIR has no loop.

name: texture-atomics-outside-1d-1d-array-2d-array-3d-buffer-and-2d-textures
rationale: Every texture atomic D283 decodes (family C), each result read at lane 0, in a kernel: thread t works on texel t of texture 0 (r32_uint 1D, 8 wide, 0x1000 + 0x111t), 1 (r32_sint 1D array, 8 wide, 2 layers, (-1)^(t+l) (20 + 3t + 50l)), 2 (r32_uint 2D array, 8x1, 2 slices, 0x2000 + 0x10t + 0x100l), 3 (r32_sint 3D, 8x1x2, (-1)^t (1000 + 37t) + 500z), 4 (r32_uint buffer, 8, 0x4000 + t), and 5 (r32_sint 2D, 8x1, -5 + 2t; 16-bit coordinates), all read_write, at layer (or slice) t & 1, and 2 from thread 9: it fetch-adds, -subs, -ands, -ors, -xors, -mins, and -maxes, exchanges, stores, loads, and compare-exchanges with a stale and then the current expected texel (lane 0 of expected read back), writing each old texel's first component (as uint), each compare-exchange's result, and the layer to out[40t .. 40t + 39] of buffer 0 (uint elements, pre-filled with 0xAB). 10 threads: threads 8 and 9 address texels 8 and 9, past every texture's width, and thread 9 layer (or slice) 2, past the arrays' and the 3D texture's last, where Metal's atomics return 0 and change nothing and a compare-exchange fails and leaves expected (D236.8, measured on 2D textures). Every texture is an out-of-bounds target; the texture buffer's 16-byte guard past it covers texels 8 and 9. The AIR has no loop.

name: unpremultiply-four-argb8-pixels-across-the-alpha-zero-guard
rationale: The half unpack/pack pair round-trips a byte exactly, so the case is byte-authorable wherever the reciprocal stays on the b/255 grid. The four alphas are chosen to do that: 255 makes the reciprocal exactly 1 and the pixel an identity; 0 takes the guarded arm and must give a fully zero pixel rather than an infinity; 51 and 85 are 255/5 and 255/3, so each colour byte divides to another whole byte (10,20,30 -> 50,100,150 and 17,34,51 -> 51,102,153) and the half rounding lands far from any packing midpoint. Component 0 is the alpha and is carried through untouched, so a shuffle that lost it would change every pixel. The row stride is 12 over a 2-pixel row, so four decoy bytes per row are never read and the matching four destination bytes must keep their seed.

name: matmul2d-cooperative-destination-layout-128x128x32-nn-half-half-float-4-simdgroup
rationale: Where Metal places the elements of matmul2d's cooperative destination tensor (DESIGN D272): descriptor 128x128x32, transpose_right false, multiply_accumulate, element types half, half, float (left, right, destination), execution scope of 4 simdgroup(s) (128 threads, one threadgroup), function constant 0 = 18. Thread t writes the capacity to out[t] and, for element i, one word at out[128 + t * capacity + i] while that index is below limit = 16384: bit 31 valid, bits 16-30 the byte offset from element 0 (found by setting every element i to i + 1 and searching the storage, read as an array of the element type from element 0, for that value; 0x7FFF when no slot below the capacity holds it), bits 0-7 and 8-15 the coordinates of a valid element; words never written keep 0xFFFFFFFF. The layout is the implementation's, but a guest may address elements by offset from element 0 (the qmm kernels fill the right input that way), so the candidate must reproduce Metal's placement exactly. Loops bounded by the capacity (expected 128; the search is capacity squared).

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-twenty-one
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 21 and receives exact float4 zero from all twenty linked _uber_clear bodies. A twenty-three-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; the final selector reads register 2 and writes exact zero to the poisoned primary texel.

name: loads-past-a-sixteen-byte-constant-buffer
rationale: Eight threads (DESIGN D225, the uniform buffer form). blk is a 16-byte constant struct (its window is bounded, so robust descriptors view it as a uniform buffer). idx = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 7, 20, 63. Thread t loads word idx[t] of blk into out[t]: threads 0 to 3 load blk's four words, threads 4 to 7 load words 4 to 63, past blk (within its 256-byte reach), whose results Metal leaves undefined: out bytes 16 to 31 are the declared out-of-bounds reads of blk. So out = blk's words, then the four reads; nothing outside out changes.

name: bounded-dynamic-visible-table-clear-slot-two-rgb-lane-output
rationale: The literal four-word size table [4, 0, 0, 0] bounds the only reachable loop: its induction starts at visible-table slot 2, increments once to 3, and exits because the masked first word minus one is exactly 3. One invocation takes the non-empty path because the authored bounds are float2(1), calls visible-function-table slot 2, and receives exact float4 zero from the linked _uber_clear body without dereferencing callback arguments. Eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds, with register 2 selected as the result. This entry splats the linked result R, G, and B lanes into three adjacent poisoned RGBA32 pixels; the complete 3x1 footprint is selected for byte-exact comparison.

name: linked-k48-gather-quantized-matrix-multiply-rhs-float-16-transposed
rationale: Reaching variant of the zero-K case of this entry (DESIGN D296; WP-EVG, TODO 6.2), whose K = 0 stops the kernel before its arithmetic. One threadgroup of 32 lanes (1 simdgroup) runs the single 16x16 output tile: B = 1, M = N = 16, K = 48 (one whole 32-deep block, the unsafe loader, and a 16-deep remainder, the safe one). The user constant keeps 8-bit unsigned weights, group size one, no bias, the non-cooperative loader; constant 122 binds a two-entry table. The indices select expert 0 for rows below 8 and expert 1 for the rest, so the kernel walks two row segments, each a full tile multiply over its expert (expert strides w, scales and biases batch stride = N*K = 768), writing only its own rows. W[e][n][k] (w_ld = 48 bytes): both experts hold q(n, k) = (11n + 3k + floor(3nk/5)) mod 16, nonlinear in n, so the column sums differ (all 16 distinct whichever scale element the layout reads); expert 0's scales repeat 0.5, 1, 2 and expert 1's are half of them (biases unread without the bias bit). x is [M][K] (x_ld = 48): rows of segment 0 hold a = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 repeating, rows of segment 1 hold 2a, so every row of the result is the same (2a . W/2 = a . W): the linked destination callback, which writes table entry 1 at the column coordinate only, stores one value per column from every row, the same value, so the 16 words observed (64 bytes) do not depend on write order, and a row given the other segment's expert would write another. Each dequantized weight is a multiple of 0.25 at most 30, exact in float, and each x at most 10; each product with x a multiple of 0.5 at most 150 and each sum of 48 at most 7200, below 2^13: exact in float in any order or contraction.

name: linked-zero-k-gather-quantized-matrix-multiply-rhs-float-16-transposed
no_effect: The authored parameters give the work an empty extent, so the entry returns before any write reaches the selected output.
rationale: The transposed float 16 counterpart of the committed mps_gather_qmm_rhs_t_bfloat_64 case (DESIGN D272): mps_gather_qmm_rhs_t_float_16 with the same function constants, resources, one-thread dispatch, and linked visible functions (postfixPrimary_4xf, postfixPrimary_f). Its zero extents keep every loop bound finite, so the case observes the four-byte destination allocation; the kernel links translation units each with its own static initializer and no llvm.global_ctors list, and calls matmul2d, so its translation exercises the unordered-initializer rule (D272.4) and the matmul2d lowering (D272.3). Replaced (DESIGN D296): the linked destination callback writes table entry 1, so the case binds a two-entry table (MPSNDArrayRefSize 1 source, 1 destination) whose destination element carries the source element's fill.

name: quad-ops-across-sixteen-quads
rationale:
Five quad families on a 64-thread one-dimensional threadgroup -- quad_sum on float4, quad_max and quad_min on a signed int, quad_broadcast and quad_shuffle_xor -- across sixteen whole quads. Each thread's datum is its own index, so every one of the 64 values is distinct and the four lanes a result came from are readable straight off the answer: quad_sum returns the sum of the four indices, which is different for every quad, and quad_broadcast of lane 2 returns the quad base plus two, which names the quad and the lane at once. The integer extrema are given 3*tid - 40, which crosses zero inside the fourth quad, so the signed comparison is exercised on both signs and an unsigned min or max would lose the negative lanes.

The threadgroup is deliberately one-dimensional. Metal groups a quad as four consecutive threads here, which is what this translator's lane-XOR butterfly computes, and both back ends agree value for value. In a kernel that also takes an imageblock Metal switches the threadgroup to a two-by-two tiled lane assignment and the quad becomes a spatial 2x2 block instead; that shape is 8 of the 14579 corpus sources and is not what this case covers.

name: linked-single-threadgroup-zero-bin
rationale: One 1x1 threadgroup dispatches one invocation. kLogBinEntries=0 makes both initialization and flush loops contain exactly one bin, kTGSizeIs256=false uses the literal one-thread group size as their stride, and source_size=1x1 bounds the image path. The exact linked callback returns float4 zero without dereferencing resources; the poisoned global bin makes the local-atomic aggregation observable byte-exactly.

name: constant-half4-render-target
rationale: The parameter-free fragment entry returns half4(1) to color attachment zero; a generated full-coverage triangle must replace every byte of the poisoned one-pixel RGBA16Float target.

name: read-a-halfword-view-of-a-uint-buffer-at-its-own-stride
rationale:
The device evidence for the byte-view path, on the pointer spelling the Metal frontend actually emits. `xcrun metal -S -emit-llvm` writes LLVM's pre-opaque pointers, so this fixture's `.ll` is the frontend's own output with only the triple rewritten -- `i32 addrspace(1)* %0`, and the two reinterprets as `bitcast i32 addrspace(1)* %p to i8 addrspace(1)*` and `... to i16 addrspace(1)*`. No other authored case is in that spelling, and no harvested source is either: all 14579 were retripled to `spirv-unknown-vulkan1.2`, which erases pointee types. A whole dialect therefore had no device evidence at all, and the corpus A/B cannot see it.

`shorts` is a halfword view taken at byte 4 of a `device uint *`, so `shorts[g]` is the halfword at byte `4 + 2*g` -- the VIEW's stride, not the buffer's. Reading the reinterpreting bitcast as a non-identity gave the halfword GEP the base's uint stride instead, addressing byte `4 + 4*g` and loading four bytes where two were meant, and it put a second `RuntimeArray<uchar>` variable on descriptor (set 0, binding 0) beside the uint one. `spirv-val` accepts both.

The input is bytes 0..127 in order, so `bytes[g] = g` and `shorts[g] = (4+2g) | (5+2g)<<8`. The two reads occupy disjoint bit fields of the result -- byte in bits 0..7, halfword in bits 16..31 -- so a byte read that stays correct proves the store landed on the right lane while the halfword moved. The stride error changes 15 of the 16 lanes (every g but 0, where 4+2g and 4+4g coincide), and it stays inside the 128-byte input, so the wrong answer is a defined value rather than an out-of-bounds read that could report as anything. The output is 128 bytes prefilled with 0xAB and compared whole while only its first 64 are written, so a store that walks off the end of the written region is visible as a lost fill.

name: imageblock-runtime-slice-region-code-plane
rationale: Five imageblock slice writes whose block extent is [[threads_per_threadgroup]] arithmetic -- a value AIR computes at runtime, not a constant the translator can read -- asked from three different cells so that where the block STARTS is answered too. air.write_imageblock_slice_to_texture_2d.i16.v4i16 (2 case-less corpus sources), air.write_imageblock_slice_to_texture_2d.f16 (1) and air.write_imageblock_slice_to_texture_2d.v4f32 (2) -- 5 sources, and the device half of the 22-source class of corpus modules whose slice region is a runtime value. The threadgroup is 8x8 and each thread owns one cell, so the imageblock is 8x8 and a lowering that took the block extent from the imageblock rather than from the size operand agrees with the first write and with nothing else: the code plane asks for tgSize >> 1, a 4x4 block, at (8, 0), and a copy sized by the imageblock would write 8x8 there and put 48 texels of tile content over the authored poison in a corner of the texture the answer never reaches. The colour plane asks for the whole tgSize block at (0, 0), the one case where the two readings agree, so a lowering copying nothing at all cannot be mistaken for one that reads the operand. The three weight writes are the origin question. They ask for the same field at three sizes from three different cells -- cell (4,4) at size 4x4 to (0,8), cell (0,0) at 2x2 to (8,8), and cell (5,3) at 1x1 to (12,12) -- and Metal answered cells (0..3,0..3), cells (0..1,0..1) and cell (0,0). Not one of them started where the pointer pointed: the block always starts at the imageblock's own origin, the pointer selects which field of the cell is copied, and its cell coordinate is ignored. The 1x1 write is what rules out a rounding or clamping story -- a copy anchored at the pointer would have answered 29 there and it answered 0. Every cell holds a value that exists nowhere else in the tile: the colour is (x, y, x/2 + 1/4, y/4 + 1/2), the code is (7x - 3, 11y - 5, 100x + y, -(x + 16y)) and the weight is x + 8y, so a transposed, swizzled or shifted copy lands a quadruple that exists nowhere in the tile at all, which is what makes the three origin rows readable as coordinates rather than as noise. Every float is an integer or an exact binary fraction below 16 and every half an integer below 64, so all are exact in their own format and the comparison needs no tolerance. The three planes carry three texel types and two coordinate types -- a ushort2 write for the codes and uint2 writes for the other two -- because the AIR symbol spells both, and a lowering reading the coordinate at the wrong width would place a whole block somewhere else. The grid is exactly one threadgroup: an explicit-layout imageblock with no implicit coverage takes the compute path, and a second tile would copy its own block to the same texture origin.
